rule.description: Report dedicated date-part codec converters (raw part value -> number decoding with a self-contained missing-part default, and Date value -> per-part display text encoding) that are defined as module-scope named exports inside JSX-bearing component owner modules instead of being owned by one shared module.

rule_target.single_location: one shared non-component module owning the date-part codec policy (both decoding fallbacks and display text encoding) that all part-view modules import
rule_target.satisfied_by: Any repair that gives these converters one shared owner (for example a parametrized part decoder/encoder keyed by part name, or a single shared module owning the policy) leaves no component owner module exporting a dedicated date-part codec implementation, and the rule goes silent. Component files may keep importing and dispatching; only converter ownership is checked.

checks.description: Detect a component owner module that exports a dedicated, module-scope 'raw part value -> number' converter which selects its own missing-part default (Number(raw || fallback), Number(raw ?? fallback), or a Number-isNaN ternary).
checks.detected_relation: JSX-bearing component module -> named export that decodes one date part while owning the fallback default for that part
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The input-decoding half of the date-part codec policy is implemented piecemeal: each part-view owner carries its own copy of the policy plus its own fallback constant, so changing the policy or a default requires editing every owner instead of one shared location.

matches.evidence: Exported by the day input component module; returns Number(rawDayValue || 1), embedding the day fallback (first of month) in the component owner.

Exported by the month input component module; returns Number(rawMonthValue || 1), embedding the month fallback (January) in the component owner and also imported by the sibling DayInput module for its days-in-month bound.
Exported by the month select component module; duplicates the same month policy a second time for the select rendering, selecting January via a Number.isNaN ternary instead of a logical default.
Exported by the year input component module; returns Number(rawYearValue || new Date().getFullYear()), embedding the current-year fallback in the component owner.

checks.description: Detect a component owner module that exports a dedicated, module-scope 'Date value -> per-part display text' converter (a single return of getX(value).toString() or String(getX(value))).
checks.detected_relation: JSX-bearing component module -> named export that encodes the current value into one part's display text
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The value-presentation half of the date-part codec policy is likewise implemented as per-owner copies: every part-view module re-derives its own string from the value, so presenting parts consistently and changing presentation policy means coordinated edits in several owners.

matches.evidence: Exported by the day input component module; returns getDate(nextValue).toString(), encoding value -> day text inside the component owner.
Exported by the month input component module; returns getMonthHuman(nextValue).toString(), encoding value -> month text inside the component owner.
Exported by the year input component module; returns getYear(nextValue).toString(), encoding value -> year text inside the component owner.

excluded.reason: Module-level strategy tables register imported converter pointers per part name; they are dispatch configuration consumed at runtime by the DateInput component, not converter implementations, so the rule intentionally does not flag them.
The DateInput component and its nested change handlers consume the codec but are not dedicated module-scope named converter exports; the rule targets converter definitions owned by component modules.
Shared numeric bound helpers are not component owner modules (no JSX) and are not date-part codec logic; they are boundaries and look similar only because of their brevity.
Shared date-interval helpers already live in a shared module and do not decode raw form values or encode display text; they never match the rule.
A cached Intl formatter lookup is not a per-part codec; excluded because it neither selects missing-part defaults nor produces per-part display strings.
Spec files are outside the analyzed production surface of this check.
